proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 7 is headed "Indemnification of Contractor" but contains no indemnity at all, so we carry third-party IP risk on work Contractor creates. We have added our standard Contractor indemnity covering IP infringement, breach of law, data incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; if helpful we can pair it with the usual exclusions (our modifications, combinations and specifications) and procure/modify/replace/refund remedies.

ops.text: (d) Contractor shall defend, indemnify and hold harmless Company and its affiliates from and against any third-party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (i) an allegation that the Services or Works infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right; (ii) Contractor's breach of applicable law; (iii) any unauthorised access to or disclosure of Company data or Confidential Information caused by Contractor; or (iv) Contractor's gross negligence or wilful misconduct. Company shall give Contractor prompt notice of the claim, Contractor shall have control of the defence, and Company shall provide reasonable cooperation at Contractor's expense. Any indemnity given by Company shall be limited to third-party claims arising from materials or content provided by Company and Company's breach of applicable law.

proposal.summary: Insert Contractor indemnity for IP, legal breach, data incidents and misconduct

quote: 7. LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.
rationale: Despite the heading, Section 7 contains no indemnity language at all — no Contractor indemnity for third-party IP claims, breach of law, data incidents or misconduct (the non-infringement representation in 5(c) is a warranty, not a defence obligation). We inserted the standard Contractor indemnity at 7(d) with notice/control/cooperation mechanics and a narrow reverse indemnity from us.
sectionRef: § 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 4 vests the Works in us but says nothing about the data and materials we supply, and Section 4(b)(ii) sweeps records "relating to the Services" to Contractor. We have added a short confirmation that we retain all rights in Company data and materials and that no rights in them transfer to Contractor.

ops.text: Company retains all right, title and interest in and to all data, content and materials provided or made available by Company or generated for Company in the course of the Services ("Company Data"), and nothing in this Agreement assigns or transfers to Contractor any ownership of Company Data or of Company's other intellectual property. No Works or Company Data shall be jointly owned.

proposal.summary: Add Company ownership of Company data and materials

quote: are the property of Company to the extent that such Works were created by Contractor for Company over a time period for which Company has been invoiced and said invoice has been paid
rationale: Works vest in us only for invoiced-and-paid periods (acceptable in principle), but the agreement never confirms that we retain ownership of the data, content and materials we supply, while Section 4(b)(ii) sweeps "records relating to the Services" into Contractor's exclusive property. We added a Company Data ownership sentence confirming no transfer of our IP or data to Contractor and no joint ownership.
ruleTitle: Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data
sectionRef: § 4 OWNERSHIP OF MATERIALS RELATED TO SERVICES; ACCEPTANCE.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We can accept a mutual cap set at the greater of 12 months' fees and USD 1,000,000, but the current cap is measured by fees paid under a single Statement of Work and carves out only a cross-reference to Paragraph 9 (which is the independent-contractor clause). Confidentiality, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement must sit outside the cap, and our payment obligations are not "damages".

ops.newText: (a) EXCEPT FOR EXCLUDED CLAIMS, EACH PARTY'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT SHALL NOT EXCEED THE GREATER OF (A) THE FEES PAID OR PAYABLE BY COMPANY UNDER THIS AGREEMENT IN THE TWELVE (12) MONTHS IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM AND (B) USD 1,000,000. "EXCLUDED CLAIMS" MEANS A PARTY'S BREACH OF ITS CONFIDENTIALITY, DATA PROTECTION OR SECURITY OBLIGATIONS, ITS INDEMNIFICATION OBLIGATIONS, ITS GROSS NEGLIGENCE, WILFUL MISCONDUCT OR FRAUD, AND ITS INFRINGEMENT OF THE OTHER PARTY'S INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY RIGHTS. COMPANY'S OBLIGATION TO PAY FEES PROPERLY DUE SHALL NOT BE TREATED AS DAMAGES SUBJECT TO THIS LIMITATION.
ops.oldText: (a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO CONTRACTOR'S OBLIGATIONS PURSUANT TO PARAGRAPH 9 HEREOF, CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES. COMPANYS' MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO CONTRACTOR FOR ANY REASON ARISING OUT OF THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR.

proposal.summary: Make cap mutual on a 12-month fee basis with standard uncapped carve-outs

quote: CONTRACTOR'S MAXIMUM LIABILITY TO COMPANY ARISING FOR ANY REASON RELATING TO CONTRACTOR'S PERFORMANCE OF SERVICES UNDER A STATEMENT OF WORK SHALL BE LIMITED TO THE AMOUNT OF FEES PAID TO CONTRACTOR FOR THE PERFORMANCE OF SUCH SERVICES.
rationale: The cap is measured by fees paid under the individual Statement of Work (potentially a very small amount), not 12 months' fees or USD 1,000,000, and the only carve-out is a broken cross-reference to "Paragraph 9", which is the Independent Contractor clause. There are no carve-outs for confidentiality, data/security, indemnification, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud or IP infringement, and our payment obligations are not excluded from the cap. Mutual exclusion of consequential damages in 7(b) is acceptable.
ruleTitle: Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs
sectionRef: § 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot be blocked from assigning to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and a change of control should not give Contractor any termination or re-pricing right. Consent for other assignments remains subject to the existing reasonableness standard.

ops.newText: Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld; provided that Company may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in connection with a merger, acquisition, reorganisation or sale of all or substantially all of its assets, and no change of control of Company shall constitute an assignment or give Contractor any right to terminate, suspend or re-price this Agreement.
ops.oldText: Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld.

proposal.summary: Add affiliate/successor assignment carve-out for Company

quote: Neither party shall assign, transfer, or subcontract this Agreement or any of its obligations hereunder without the other party's express, prior written consent, which will not be unreasonably withheld.
rationale: The mutual consent requirement has no carve-out allowing us to assign to an affiliate or to a successor in an M&A transaction, and the agreement is silent on change of control. We added the affiliate/successor carve-out and confirmed that a change of control of Company is not an assignment and gives Contractor no termination or re-pricing right.
sectionRef: § 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

quote: Company agrees to retain Contractor to perform the consulting services for Company, on a task by task basis (the "Services")
rationale: The engagement is task-by-task under Statements of Work with no sole-source, exclusivity or "all requirements" language binding us; we remain free to use other suppliers.

quote: Contractor shall be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination.
rationale: On termination we pay only fees and expenses actually incurred or earned; there are no liquidated damages, penalties, minimum termination fees or late-payment interest payable by us. Section 5 in fact allows us to withhold fees on an anti-bribery termination, which is in our favour.
ruleTitle: Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The licence to Contractor Information embedded in the Works must be irrevocable and must cover our affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf, and transfer to a successor; otherwise the Works we paid for cannot be used across our group.

ops.newText: Contractor hereby grants to Company and its affiliates and contractors acting on Company's behalf a royalty-free, non- exclusive, worldwide, perpetual and irrevocable license (including the right to grant a sublicense, and transferable to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
ops.oldText: Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.

proposal.summary: Make embedded-IP licence irrevocable and extend to affiliates and contractors

quote: Contractor hereby grants to Company a royalty-free, non- exclusive perpetual license (including the right to grant a sublicense) to use, copy, modify, create, derivative version, publicly perform and publicly display such Contractor's Information in connection with Company's business operations.
rationale: The licence to Contractor Information embedded in the Works is perpetual and sublicensable but is not stated to be irrevocable or worldwide, does not name our affiliates or contractors acting on our behalf, and is not transferable to a successor. We made those minimal additions so the Works we pay for can be used across our group.
sectionRef: § 4 OWNERSHIP OF MATERIALS RELATED TO SERVICES; ACCEPTANCE.

quote: Company acknowledges that Contractor provides consulting and development services to other clients, and agrees that nothing in this Agreement shall be deemed or construed to prevent Contractor from delivering on such business.
rationale: No non-compete or field-of-use restriction binds us. Section 4(b) preserves Contractor's freedom to serve other clients, which is a restriction-free provision from our side; the only limit on us is a use restriction on Contractor's own proprietary materials, not a restraint on our business.
sectionRef: § 4 OWNERSHIP OF MATERIALS RELATED TO SERVICES; ACCEPTANCE.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] As drafted, neither party may terminate for convenience while a Statement of Work is open, so we are locked in, while Contractor can walk on 15 days' notice between SOWs. We need a 30-day convenience right (including for any SOW) with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, and Contractor should not be able to abandon an open Statement of Work for convenience.

ops.newText: (a) Company may terminate this Agreement or any Statement of Work for convenience, in whole or in part, for any or no reason upon thirty (30) days advance written notice to Contractor, in which case Contractor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination and no early-termination fee or penalty shall be payable. At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, Contractor may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon ninety (90) days advance notice to Company.
ops.oldText: (a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.

proposal.summary: Give Company convenience termination during an SOW; restrict Contractor's

quote: (a) At any time that there is no uncompleted Statement of Work outstanding, either party may terminate this Agreement for any or no reason upon fifteen (15) days advance notice to the other.
rationale: Convenience termination is available only when no Statement of Work is outstanding, so we have no exit from live engagements, and Contractor may walk on just 15 days' notice. We added a 30-day Company convenience right (covering any Statement of Work) with a pro-rata refund and no penalty, and moved Contractor's convenience right to 90 days between engagements.

quote: Contractor shall bill Company as set forth in the relevant Statement of Work. Each invoice submitted by Contractor will provide supporting detail for the Services invoiced
rationale: There are no audit, inspection or verification rights running against us — the records flow the other way (Contractor must supply supporting detail with invoices), and there is no Contractor right of access to our systems. Nothing to redline.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Arizona law is outside our approved list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), and disputes should go to courts rather than private arbitration under the USAM rules. We have set New York law with exclusive jurisdiction in New York County; Delaware or California would also work if Arizona is a problem for you.

ops.newText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof, and each party submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.
ops.oldText: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.

ops.newText: will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York.
ops.oldText: will be subject to and resolved by binding arbitration pursuant to the Arbitration Rules of U.S. Arbitration & Mediation, (www.usam.com).

proposal.summary: Move governing law and venue to New York courts

quote: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Arizona, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof.
rationale: Arizona law is outside our approved list (New York, Delaware, California, England and Wales), and Section 19 imposes mandatory binding arbitration under the U.S. Arbitration & Mediation rules with no agreed seat, whereas our position is court resolution. We replaced the governing law with New York and set exclusive jurisdiction in the New York County courts in both places; Delaware or California is our fallback.
sectionRef: § 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

quote: During the term of this Agreement, Company agrees to compensate Contractor as set forth in each Statement of Work.
rationale: The compensation provisions contain no most-favoured-nation or best-terms obligation running against us (nor in our favour). Nothing to redline under this rule; note separately that Contractor may change rates on 30 days' notice, which we address commercially.

quote: Contractor will be compensated on a time and materials.
rationale: Compensation is time-and-materials under individual Statements of Work with no minimum purchase, retainer floor, take-or-pay or shortfall mechanic and no volume caps on us. Nothing to redline.
ruleTitle: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

proposal.comment: [Playbook] The mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel involved in the Services is acceptable, but it needs the standard carve-out for general advertising and unsolicited approaches so ordinary recruitment activity is not caught.

ops.newText: without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld. This restriction shall not apply to general advertisements or other recruitment efforts not specifically targeted at the other party's personnel, or to the hiring of any person who approaches a party on an unsolicited basis or who responds to such general advertisement.
ops.oldText: without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.

proposal.summary: Add general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-out to the mutual non-solicit

quote: Neither party shall, during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination, solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services, without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld.
rationale: The non-solicit is mutual, 12 months and limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, which meets our fallback except that it lacks a carve-out for general advertising and unsolicited approaches; "solicit for hire ... or otherwise" could otherwise capture ordinary recruitment. We added the standard carve-out sentence.
sectionRef: § 7 LIMITATIONS OF LIABILITY; INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR.

quote: 2. TERM. The term of this Agreement shall begin on the date hereof and shall continue until terminated by either party pursuant to Paragraph 6 hereof.
rationale: The term is evergreen-until-terminated with no automatic renewal term, no non-renewal notice window and no renewal price uplift mechanic, so there is nothing to shorten or cap under this rule (rate changes are handled as a pricing point in Section 3(b)).

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 6 says nothing about wind-down, so on exit we have no right to our data back or to help migrating. We have added our standard six-month transition assistance at your then-current rates plus return of Company data within 30 days and certified deletion; 90 days of assistance would be our fallback.

ops.text: (d) Upon expiry or termination of this Agreement or any Statement of Work for any reason, Contractor shall (i) at Company's request, provide reasonable transition assistance for up to six (6) months at Contractor's then-current rates; (ii) within thirty (30) days, return to Company all Works, Company data and Confidential Information in a commonly used, machine-readable format; and (iii) thereafter delete such materials from its systems and certify such deletion in writing.

proposal.summary: Insert transition assistance and data return/deletion obligations

quote: Upon any such termination, Contractor will be paid all fees and expenses that have been incurred or earned in connection with the performance of the Services through the effective date of such termination. Contractor shall provide to Company, and hereby assigns to Company, all right, title and interest to any Works in progress.
rationale: Termination only addresses payment and assignment of Works in progress — there is no transition assistance, no obligation to return our data or Confidential Information in a usable format and no deletion/certification obligation. We inserted a wind-down paragraph at 6(d) (six months' assistance at then-current rates, 30-day data return, certified deletion).
ruleTitle: Post-termination transition assistance and data return

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 5 gives us authority, legal-compliance and non-infringement warranties but no warranty that the Works conform to the Specifications and no remedy, so the disclaimer in 5(e) leaves us without recourse for defective work. We have added a 90-day conformity warranty (12 months for software is our preference) with re-performance, repair or refund.

ops.text: Contractor further represents and warrants that (i) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; (ii) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery (twelve (12) months in the case of software), each Work will conform in all material respects to the applicable Specifications and documentation; and (iii) the Works will contain no viruses or other malicious code. Company's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Contractor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Works.

proposal.summary: Add conformity warranty with remedy and protect it from the disclaimer

quote: THE EXPRESS WARRANTIES IN THIS AGREEMENT SHALL BE IN LIEU OF ALL OTHER WARRANTIES, EXPRESS OR IMPLIED, INCLUDING THE IMPLIED WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE.
rationale: Section 5 gives only authority, legal-compliance and non-infringement representations — there is no warranty that the Works conform to the Specifications, no warranty period and no repair/re-perform/refund remedy, while 5(e) disclaims all implied warranties. We inserted a 90-day conformity warranty (12 months for software), a workmanlike-performance warranty, no-malicious-code and the standard remedy.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] Contractor handles our Confidential Information and systems, so we need cyber/privacy cover (USD 5M preferred, USD 2M as a fallback) and E&O at USD 2M with a USD 2M general liability aggregate; the workers' compensation and certificate language is unchanged.

ops.newText: comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) per occurrence and two million dollars ($2,000,000) in the aggregate, professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least two million dollars ($2,000,000), and cyber and privacy liability insurance with coverage of at least five million dollars ($5,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services
ops.oldText: comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000), in connection with the provision of Services

proposal.summary: Raise E&O and add cyber liability cover

quote: comprehensive general liability insurance with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000) and professional errors and omissions insurance for bodily injury, property damage or other losses with coverage of at least one million dollars ($1,000,000)
rationale: An insurance clause exists with workers' compensation, USD 1M CGL and USD 1M E&O, but there is no cyber/privacy cover even though Contractor handles our Confidential Information and may access our systems, and there is no CGL aggregate. We raised E&O to USD 2M, added a USD 2M aggregate and added cyber liability cover (USD 5M preferred, USD 2M fallback).
